name: MIAMI INTERNATIONAL HOLDINGS

priced.reason: book method needs rotce_override or final_growth

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That I am refusing a name the engine has merely mis-signed, when the fix is obvious and one line long: substitute a current return for the stale three-year average. The company reports $0.47 of GAAP diluted EPS for the quarter, so annualised return on $6.53 of tangible book is on the order of 25-29%, and at a 9.6% cost of equity the Gordon form would give a justified multiple far above the actual 4.81 and call the name cheap. On that reading the defect is the window, not the method, and the SLDE precedent applies — a flag that misfires on a genuine case should not be allowed to veto the whole name.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Whether tangible common equity is a CAPITAL CONSTRAINT on MIAX writing more business, which is the separator the SLDE entry establishes. For an insurer or a lender it is: regulatory capital limits the book. For an exchange it is not — order flow is limited by technology, latency, fee schedules and member relationships, and the clearing risk sits with the OCC rather than on MIAX's balance sheet. The test is whether revenue growth has required equity growth, and the Q3 numbers say the opposite: net revenue grew 20% while adjusted expenses FELL year over year and margin expanded more than 1,000 basis points, which is the signature of an asset-light platform, not of a capital-constrained balance sheet.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Yes, and it defeats the counter. The arithmetic the counter proposes would produce a large positive gap, but it would be an answer to the wrong question: a 25-29% 'return on tangible equity' on a business whose equity is a working-capital balance is not a return on anything economically meaningful, and the Gordon form becomes arbitrarily sensitive as the numerator rises — exactly the PIPR failure, where a payments and advisory cohort produced justified multiples that were meaningless in both directions. The `rotce_suggests_asset_light_financial` separator comes out on the refuse side here: tangible equity is a residual, not a constraint. I note the `goodwill_and_intangibles_26%_of_book` flag is the model fighting itself in the same way — those intangibles ARE the exchange technology generating the fees, and stripping them to reach 'tangible' book deletes the productive asset before dividing by it.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Why the stock has fallen 33.2% in 63 days on improving fundamentals. The most likely explanations are post-listing share supply — including continuing warrant exercises at $5.50 and $26.00 strikes — and multiple compression from a high initial rating, but I could not establish it from the filings I read and the news store holds nothing on this company after 2026-09-25. I also did not read the updated full-year adjusted operating expense guidance range in full, so I cannot say whether the 10.1% five-day fall is a reaction to an expense guide-up alongside the revenue beat. And I did not quantify the remaining warrant overhang, which is the one dilution channel that is demonstrably live.

what_changed: The Q3 2026 earnings release landed 2026-10-29, the day before this pass, and the engine's extract is built on the 2026-06-30 balance sheet. Net revenue $131.0M (+20%), adjusted EBITDA $70.8M (+47%) at a 54% margin, GAAP diluted EPS $0.47, adjusted diluted EPS $0.45, options average daily volume 11.1 million contracts (+15%), options market share 17.4%, adjusted expenses below the prior year, and updated full-year 2026 adjusted operating expense guidance. Management describes a 'next growth phase' with Bloomberg index futures now on NinjaTrader and four fertilizer futures contracts launched. Separately and materially: the Nasdaq litigation, first brought on 2017-09-01 and running nine years, was dismissed with prejudice on 2026-07-20 after the PTAB invalidated six of the asserted patents in 2019 — all claims and counterclaims resolved, with MIAX confirmed free to operate and license without Nasdaq consent. And a 2026-06-22 item 3.02 discloses 1,881,554 shares issued since 1 April 2026 on warrant exercises at $5.50 and $26.00 strikes, including the surrender of 2,362,279 warrants under an exchange agreement — an ongoing dilution channel rather than a one-off.
consensus_case: Miami International Holdings is an exchange operator, and at $31.44 the market is paying roughly 17x annualised adjusted earnings for a business that grew net revenue 20% year over year to $131.0M in the third quarter, lifted adjusted EBITDA 47% to $70.8M at a 54% margin — more than 1,000 basis points of margin expansion — and took options market share to 17.4% on average daily volume of 11.1 million contracts, up 15%. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.47 and adjusted $0.45. On 2026-07-20 the US District Court for New Jersey dismissed with prejudice the nine-year Nasdaq patent litigation, leaving MIAX 'free to operate its business without any license or consent being required from Nasdaq' and free to build new exchanges and license its technology — a structural overhang removed, not settled. Against that, the stock is down 33.2% over 63 days and 10.1% over five, which on these numbers looks like post-listing share supply and multiple compression rather than deterioration: warrants struck at $5.50 and $26.00 continue to be exercised (1,881,554 shares issued between April and 17 June 2026 alone), and the company has just updated full-year adjusted operating expense guidance. None of that is what this brief is pricing.
base_case_rationale: No sustainable ROTCE can honestly be supplied, because price to tangible book is the wrong model for this business and supplying a return would launder that category error into a fair value. MIAX is a technology-driven exchange operator: its productive assets are matching-engine software, SEC exchange licences, member relationships and order flow, which are either expensed as incurred or carried as intangibles that the tangible-book construction then strips out before dividing. The brief's own numbers say so — actual price to tangible book of 4.81 against tangible book of $6.53 a share, where the standing lesson sets roughly 4x as the signature of a company whose capital is not its balance sheet. A 54% adjusted EBITDA margin on $131M of quarterly revenue is not a return on $6.53 of tangible equity in any meaningful sense. The model compounds that with a numerator defect: the 'sustainable ROTCE' of -10.8% is a three-year GAAP average carrying `loss_year_in_window`, and MIAX only listed recently, so the window spans the pre-profitability years of an exchange build-out. The company earning $0.47 of GAAP diluted EPS this quarter is not the company that average describes. That negative return then produces a justified multiple of -1.67, i.e. the model asserts the equity is worth less than nothing, against a business with 54% margins and 20% revenue growth.
key_risks: Price to tangible book of 4.81 on a book-method name is the documented signature of a business whose capital is not its balance sheet — an exchange operator's assets are licences, technology and order flow, which the tangible-book construction strips out before dividing

The 'sustainable ROTCE' of -10.8% is a three-year GAAP average carrying loss_year_in_window on a company that listed recently, so it describes the pre-profitability exchange build-out rather than the business now earning a 54% adjusted EBITDA margin
The resulting justified multiple of -1.67 asserts the equity is worth less than nothing, and the -134.8% gap and 8th-percentile cohort rank are both artifacts of that
Cost of equity rests on a sector-median beta of 0.85 standing in for a regression with an R-squared of 0.027 (raw 0.48), so the discount rate is not a measurement either
A live warrant overhang: 1,881,554 shares issued between 1 April and 17 June 2026 on exercises at $5.50 and $26.00 strikes, well below the current price
The stock is down 33.2% over 63 days on improving results, and I could not establish why from free sources
watch_for: Options market share against the 17.4% reported, and whether the 15% average-daily-volume growth holds as incumbents respond
The size of the remaining warrant overhang and the pace of further item 3.02 issuances
Whether the 54% adjusted EBITDA margin holds as the new futures products (Bloomberg index futures, the four fertilizer contracts) are built out
A full fiscal year of profitability in the extract, which is what would eventually make a return-based model arguable — though price to tangible book would still be the wrong frame
Any explanation for the 63-day decline: lock-up expiry, secondary offering, or index-related flow
